subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose child-topic native subagent session spawning now, and should that be done through the open per-kind capability work while keeping normal Telegram top-level placement as current?
rationale: Current main has generic binding primitives, but the remaining behavior affects visible Telegram topic creation, plugin capability/API shape, and session/message routing defaults.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review findings, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep Telegram current-conversation binding only and leave this issue open until maintainers decide the visibility and API model for child topics.

options.title: Reject Telegram child-topic subagent spawning
options.body: Close this issue and the active candidate PRs as not planned if maintainers decide internal subagent work should never create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review findings, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice sits at the core thread-binding policy and Telegram channel boundary that his recent merged refactor owns.
